table.title: Kimjang season by region
table.note: Normal dates come from Weatheri's table of normal kimjang dates. 'This forecast' is the first of 3 consecutive suitable days within about 9 forecast days.

criterion.title: The guideline
items: The Korea Meteorological Administration considers it kimjang season once the daily mean temperature stays at or below 4°C and the low at or below 0°C.
Kimchi made while it is warm ripens and sours quickly; once it gets too cold, cabbage and radish can freeze and lose flavor.
It is a reference based on normals, short- and mid-range forecasts and the monthly outlook. Being off by a day or two will not ruin your kimchi.

method.title: How this page calculates
items: Daily mean and low temperatures come from MET Norway city forecasts, about 9 days ahead.
A single cold day does not count as "staying" cold. The season starts on the first of 3 consecutive suitable days.
Results can differ from any separate KMA announcement. For dates beyond the forecast, use the normal date.

prep.title: Once you pick a date
items: Use the kimjang calculator to list ingredients and cost for your number of cabbages.
If you buy pre-salted cabbage, make the seasoning a day before so you can mix it on arrival.
Mix 2–3 cabbages first, taste, then adjust with salted seafood or salt.
Leave kimchi you will eat soon at room temperature for about a day; refrigerate long-keeping kimchi right away.

trend.title: Normal kimjang dates
items: Chuncheon is mid-November; Suwon, Cheongju, Seosan and Seoul late November; Incheon, Daejeon and Jeonju early December.
Daegu is early December; Gwangju and Gangneung mid-December; Ulsan, Mokpo and Yeosu late December; Busan early January.
The season is getting later as temperatures rise: Seoul's date moved from about Nov 25 (1920–1950 average) to about Nov 29 (1981–2010).

items.q: When should I make kimjang in 2026?
items.a: It depends on the region. Normal dates are about Nov 29 for Seoul, Dec 1 for Daejeon, Dec 5 for Daegu, Dec 11 for Gwangju and Jan 2 for Busan. Pick a region to see whether this year's season starts within about 9 forecast days.

items.q: When is kimjang season in Seoul?
items.a: The normal date for Seoul is around Nov 29. Southern Gyeonggi (Suwon) is around Nov 26 and Incheon around Dec 1.
KMA considers it kimjang season once the daily mean stays at or below 4°C and the low at or below 0°C. This page starts the season on the first of 3 consecutive days meeting both.

items.q: Can I make kimchi on a single cold day?
items.a: If it warms up again after a brief cold snap, kimchi can ripen quickly. That is why single days are only marked "Suitable" in the daily list, not counted as the start.

items.q: The forecast and normal date disagree. Which should I trust?
items.a: For the next few days, the forecast is more accurate. For dates beyond about 9 days, use the normal date and check the forecast again 2–3 days before.

items.q: What about the south and Jeju?
items.a: Normal dates are about Dec 25 for Mokpo, Dec 30 for Yeosu and Jan 2 for Busan. Jeju is not listed because the source table has no normal date for it.
